text:
## Season so far

Amon-Ra St. Brown is the Lions' clear No. 1 receiver. He has 114.5 half-PPR points (16.4 per game) over 7 games, on 76 targets, 53 catches, 571 yards and 5 touchdowns. His 31% target share and 84% snap rate are elite.

The season has had two phases. In Weeks 1–2 he scored 23.7 and 30.7 on 27 targets and four touchdowns, with a 142-yard game against Buffalo. After that came a lull. He scored 9.9, 11.5 and 9.9 in Weeks 3–5, with no touchdowns in the last two. He rebounded with 19.7 in Week 7 (9 catches, 153 yards) but dropped to 9.1 against Minnesota. That was his lowest scoring week, and his snaps fell to 72%, which fits the rib issue below. He has had at least 8 targets every week, so the dips were about efficiency and touchdowns, not role.

## Usage and efficiency

His season line is 7.5 yards per target. Over the last 4 games that is 8.4, and his per-game scoring is down to 12.5 from 16.4. He has no rushing role to speak of (2 carries, 9 yards). He is a pure target-earner.

The last-4 table shows what changed:
- **Target share:** 30%, against 31% for the season.
- **Snaps:** 83%, against 84%.
- **Targets:** 41 over 4 games, about 10 a game.
- **Touchdowns:** none in the last 4, after 5 in the first 3.

His usage is intact, and the drop in points comes from the touchdowns. His season total of 5 touchdowns is close to the 5.4 expected from where his targets came. He has 16 red-zone targets (7 in the last 4) and 5 goal-line targets (2 in the last 4). That is a healthy diet, and it should produce touchdowns again.

## Health and situation

He is questionable with a rib injury. He was limited in practice Wednesday and again Thursday, and the team's site tied it to his brief trip to the sideline against Minnesota. A limited Thursday session with a Friday chance to upgrade is a common pattern for players who then suit up. Rib problems (bruises or strains) generally cost players little time. The usual risk is that the player is sore and a hard hit sets him back, which can cost some snaps or production in the first game back. I could not find a verified 2026 Week 9 update beyond that. I'm treating the practice reports as the status and not assuming a diagnosis or a timetable.

The WR room has no major absences. Jameson Williams is at 20% target share over the last 4 games, 18% for the season and 89% of snaps. Isaac TeSlaa is at 11% and missed the last game, so he is a bit player when healthy. Tom Kennedy is on IR, and Tay Martin and DeAndre Carter barely play. If Amon-Ra misses time or is limited, Williams is the main beneficiary. No other receiver has the share to absorb his 30%.

## Outlook

Rest of season he projects at 133.4 points over 9 games, or 15.2 per game. The schedule factor is 0.99 and the usage trend is ×0.98. The upcoming matchups are:
- **Week 9 @ MIA:** tough.
- **Week 10 vs NE:** easy.
- **Week 11 vs TB:** tough.
- **Week 12 vs CHI:** neutral.

His floor is around 9–10 points, which he has already hit four times. His ceiling is 25–30 on a touchdown-heavy day, as in Weeks 1–2.

**Verdict: hold, and keep starting him as a weekly WR1.** I would not sell after a quiet touchdown stretch. His usage is steady, his red-zone work is real and his touchdown luck is neutral. The only open question is Friday's report. If he is a true game-time decision for Miami, have a fallback ready. If he is active, play him. Week 10 against New England is the best spot on the near-term schedule.
